title: tenant-snapshot-and-safe-replay-runbook-2026
author: Aisha Ramirez
body:
Summary:

This runbook describes the approved, auditable process for capturing production-like snapshots of a tenant (configuration + sanitized telemetry + optional minimal payloads) and safely replaying traffic in a controlled sandbox for debugging hard-to-reproduce issues. The goal is to enable Customer Success and Support to reproduce customer-facing failures while minimizing data exposure and preserving customer SLAs and compliance commitments.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and to hosted tenants where customer consent and legal approvals are present.
- Intended for escalations where live debugging is not possible (non-deterministic model regressions, KV-cache corruption, routing anomalies, telemetry sampling gaps, prefix-caching defects).
- Excludes full PII exports; any snapshot containing sensitive data must be redacted per the Data Handling section below.

Owner & Roles:
- Requestor: Customer Success or Support engineer who opened the escalation (owner of the ticket).
- Data Guardian: Security & Compliance engineer responsible for approving redaction and retention policy for the snapshot.
- Sandbox Operator: Platform engineer who performs the capture and replay steps.
- Observability Lead: Owner of tenant telemetry dashboards who validates that replay data surfaced expected signals.

SLO / Safety Requirements:
- Snapshot requests must be approved within 4 business hours for Sev2 and within 24 business hours for Sev3 after ticket triage.
- Replays must not be performed against production model endpoints. Replays occur in an isolated sandbox (no egress to customer endpoints).
- All artifacts stored in snapshot buckets expire automatically within 30 days; retention extensions require Data Guardian sign-off.
- Audit records (who requested, who approved, who executed) must be recorded in the ticket and the snapshot metadata.

Prerequisites & Approvals:
1. Customer consent recorded in the ticket (link to signed form or email).
2. Data Guardian approval if snapshot includes any of the following fields: email, ssn, phone, or free-text fields longer than 2k characters.
3. Sandbox namespace and replay cluster provisioned (see Commands section).
4. Dry-run of redaction script must pass local test vectors before execution.

Data Handling & Privacy Controls:
- Redaction-first policy: before any storage or transfer, run the redaction pipeline. Redaction steps: mask_email, pseudonymize_ids, remove_attachments, truncate_large_text.
- Redaction tool: redwood-data-sanitize v1.3 (see example below).
- Pseudonymization: replace tenant_user_id with deterministic salt keyed by tenant-id to allow joinability within the replay but not to reidentify the user set.
- Access control: snapshot buckets use encryption (KMS) and are only accessible by the Data Guardian and Sandbox Operator principals for the duration of the retention window.

Runbook: Capture a tenant snapshot (step-by-step)
1) Open a ticket and collect approvals (see Prerequisites).
2) Create snapshot job:
```bash
# create job metadata in support-api
support-cli snapshots create --tenant-id=tenant-123 --reason="Investigate intermittent truncation" --duration-days=30 --notify="#cust-success-ops"
```
- This registers the snapshot request and assigns an id (SNAP-<id>).

3) Run redaction pipeline against a streaming export (managed by telemetry exporter):
```bash
telemetry-exporter stream --tenant tenant-123 --from="2026-06-20T00:00:00Z" --to="2026-06-20T01:00:00Z" | \ 
  redwood-data-sanitize --policy minimal --salt="tenant-123-salt" > /tmp/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl
```
- The policy flags available: minimal, default, strict (strict removes nearly all free-text fields). Default should be avoided without Data Guardian approval.

4) Validate sanitization: run the snapshot validator which checks for residual PII markers and for field size anomalies.
```bash
snapshot-validator /tmp/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl --check-pii --check-length
```
- Validator returns non-zero on issues; resolve them before proceeding.

5) Upload to secure bucket:
```bash
aws s3 cp /tmp/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl s3://redwood-snapshots/tenant-123/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl --sse aws:kms --tagging "retention=30d,requestor=alice"
```
- File metadata in support-api: link to S3 object, retention expiry, approvers.

Runbook: Safe replay (isolated sandbox)
1) Provision sandbox replay cluster (if not already available for tenant): request via infra-ops-runbook. Typical cluster name pattern: replay-tenant-123-<shortid>.
2) Load snapshot into replay environment:
```bash
replayctl create --name=replay-tenant-123-01 --snapshot=s3://redwood-snapshots/tenant-123/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl --model-variant=redwood/ggml-13b-q4_0 --no-external-io
```
- --no-external-io enforces that any external callbacks are disabled in the runtime layer.

3) Execute replay scenario sets (start with conservative traffic profile):
```bash
replayctl run --name=replay-tenant-123-01 --traffic-profile=conservative --duration=15m --trace=on
```
- Traffic profiles defined: conservative (10% of peak QPS), nominal (30%), aggressive (70%); aggressive requires Observability Lead sign-off.

4) Observe telemetry and capture diffs: validate tokenization traces, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), KV-cache hit ratios, model logits diffs exported to /tmp/replay-diffs.json.

Decision matrix: When to escalate after replay
- If replay reproduces incident: open RCA path and schedule a model/serve fix with engineering. Attach replay artifacts, diffs, and sanitized logs.
- If replay does not reproduce: increase traffic conservatively (one step) and re-run once. If still not reproducible, capture a second, longer snapshot (no more than 2x duration) with approver consent.
- If redaction fails to meet compliance checks: stop and escalate to Security & Compliance; do not store or forward the artifact.

Rollback & Clean-up
- After troubleshooting completes, the Sandbox Operator must delete the replay cluster and all ephemeral compute and then mark the snapshot as archived.
- Archival: snapshot objects remain in S3 until retention expiry. To remove early: Data Guardian must sign removal request.
- Deletion steps (example):
```bash
replayctl destroy --name=replay-tenant-123-01 || true
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-snapshots/tenant-123/SNAP-SNAPID.jsonl
```
- Record deletion confirmation in the ticket with timestamps and operator identity.

Audit & Logging
- All snapshot actions produce an audit entry in the support-api: create, approve, sanitize, upload, replay-start, replay-end, destroy.
- Tickets must include the snapshot id and KMS key id used for encryption.

Common failure modes & mitigations
- Sanitizer rejects edge-case attachments: convert attachments to metadata-only and reference a stub file; escalate to Data Guardian if attachments are required for repro.
- Model variant mismatch: use the model-variant-matrix to choose a closest compatible variant; note differences in result artifacts.
- Replays diverge due to random seeds: run with seed fixed when available (replayctl --seed=42).

Checklist (pre-playback)
- [ ] Ticket has customer consent link.
- [ ] Data Guardian approval recorded.
- [ ] Redaction pipeline run and validator OK.
- [ ] Snapshot uploaded to KMS-encrypted bucket.
- [ ] Replay cluster provisioned and network-isolated.
- [ ] Observability dashboard configured for replay traces.

Commands & Example Configs
- Redaction config snippet (YAML):
```yaml
policy: minimal
fields:
  - mask_email
  - pseudonymize: [tenant_user_id]
  - truncate: {field: user_input, max_chars: 2000}
```
- Replay traffic profile JSON (example):
```json
{
  "name": "conservative",
  "qps_multiplier": 0.1,
  "arrival_process": "poisson"
}
```

Appendix: Quick play example (minimal reproduction)
1) request snapshot: support-cli snapshots create ... -> SNAP-42
2) export + sanitize -> /tmp/SNAP-42.jsonl
3) upload -> s3://redwood-snapshots/tenant-foo/SNAP-42.jsonl
4) create replay -> replayctl create --name=tmp-replay --snapshot=... --no-external-io
5) run conservative profile and collect diffs

This runbook is intended to be used verbatim when possible. Where local or customer-specific policies diverge, follow the stricter control. If any step is unclear, contact the Security & Compliance Data Guardian before proceeding.
